description: What an unreadable relevance score is, on every platform (the apps' port of bmlib's rule): a model's reply either carries a whole-number score from 1 to 5 or it carries none, and a reply with none is a parse failure that the caller retries or records, never a score. Read by tests/test_score_parity.py, Packages/BioMedLit ScoreParityTests and Android ResponseParserTest. A case gives the raw model reply and the score read from it, or null. The rules: an integer, an integral float (4.0) or a string of the ASCII digits 0-9 (" 4 ") on the scale is that score, read from the first balanced {...} in the reply (prose or a markdown fence around it is allowed, and a brace inside a JSON string is text); anything else is null and is never clamped, defaulted or rounded: off the scale (0, 6, -3, 42), a boolean, a fractional number (2.5), a word, null, a missing key, a float too large for an integer (1e300), a reply with no JSON object, a digit outside ASCII (Arabic-Indic, full-width, superscript). A reply holding NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, a number that overflows binary64 (1e999), an integer past it or a lone surrogate escape (\ud800) anywhere is unreadable as a whole, never scored by the fields beside it, also when the object is otherwise malformed (a trailing comma, a reply cut short) (#761, bmlib#572); a quoted "NaN" is text. The desktop decodes with bmlib's strict_json_loads, iOS with JSONSerialization, Android checks every number and string the lenient parse kept, and every bare token outside a string when that parse fails; none falls back to a regex or prose score after such a refusal. Desktop-only divergence: the desktop also reads a score stated in prose ('Score: 4/5') when the reply is not a JSON object; the apps do not, so no case here carries a score in prose.
